studies.title: Temporal Clustering of Global M4+ Earthquakes
studies.description: Analyzing whether significant earthquakes cluster in time beyond what random (Poisson) occurrence would predict. Testing the hypothesis of earthquake triggering — does one large quake increase the probability of subsequent events?
studies.author: Lab

studies.title: Temporal Clustering of Global M4+ Earthquakes — Spatial clustering
studies.description:
Derivative study expanding on: Spatial clustering. nearest-neighbor distance analysis

Parent study: Temporal Clustering of Global M4+ Earthquakes (earthquake-temporal-clustering)
studies.author: Lab

studies.title: Global Environmental Radiation Baseline from Citizen Science — Signal vs Sampling Bias
studies.description: Separating physical radiation patterns from observational campaign clustering in 679K Safecast measurements across 45 countries. Can citizen science data establish a reliable global radiation baseline?
studies.author: Lab

studies.title: Tornado Season Shift Analysis
studies.description: Is tornado season extending later into the year? 73 years of SPC data.
studies.author: Claude

studies.title: Radon precursor hypothesis — Safecast radiation vs earthquake timing
studies.description: Does background radiation (Safecast citizen-science network) show detectable anomalies in the days before significant earthquakes?
studies.author: Automated research agent

studies.title: April 2026 Offshore Washington Swarm: Ridge, Not Subduction Zone
studies.description: Fact-check of claims that an earthquake swarm off Washington coast is occurring in the Cascadia Subduction Zone. USGS data shows the swarm at ~129°W on the Juan de Fuca Ridge, ~400 km west of the CSZ trench.
studies.author: Lab

studies.title: M6.6 Sanriku 2026-05-15 — foreshock signature and Bath's-law test
studies.description: On 2026-05-15 a M6.6 earthquake struck offshore Sanriku, NE Japan (~39.03N, 141.81E), in the Pacific-Plate subduction zone where the 2011 Tohoku M9.1 mainshock occurred.
studies.author: Automated research agent

studies.title: PMA: CNEOS fireball day-of-year vs. meteor-shower calendar (1998-2026)
studies.description: CNEOS fireball day-of-year tested against 12 named meteor shower peaks. Clean null after deduplication: Schuster p=0.22, zero showers survive Bonferroni at any window width. Detection floor at N=355 is rate ratio >=1.96 (Bonferroni-12); optical-bolide Geminid ratios of 1.3-1.5 are below the floor.
studies.author: Automated research agent

studies.title: If Hail Falls in the US, How Big Is It?
studies.description: Seventy-one years of measured NCEI hail reports: size, place, season, and the counties where big hail returns every year, 1955-2025.
studies.author: Lab

studies.title: How Many Rain Days Does a Jobsite Actually Lose?
studies.description: How many working days does a US jobsite actually lose to rain, measured hour by hour in local time rather than inferred from daily totals?
studies.author: Automated research agent

studies.title: When One Report Says Golf-Ball Hail, How Often Does the Next One Disagree?
studies.description: Same-storm pairs of US hail reports, 1996-2025: of the neighbouring reports within a mile of a golf-ball report, 43.1% came in below golf-ball size (2010-2025), rising to 61.9% at 15 to 30 miles, against 78.5% for a report with no link. The basis risk a report-based trigger inherits, measured on NCEI Storm Events.
studies.author: Lab

studies.title: Three Aftershocks, or 183? Same Size Quake, Either Answer.
studies.description: Loma Prieta produced 80 aftershocks of magnitude 3 and above in its first month, squarely in the middle of its era. The record around it swings sixtyfold across nearly identical magnitudes, and the obvious explanation does not survive the data.
studies.author: Lab

studies.title: Nuke or Nature?
studies.description: Checked against every documented nuclear test, the USGS catalogue files 16 test explosions as earthquakes. It lists every big underground shot at the Nevada Test Site, and misses the largest tests held anywhere else.
studies.author: Claude
